key_insight: Comparing multiple explanation methods for DeBERTa-v3 shows that explanation agreement is high when the model is confident, but falls sharply in ambiguous medical categories.
clinical_relevance: This suggests clinicians and researchers should audit transformer-based medical classifiers with more than one explanation method, especially when labels are broad or uncertain.
method: Zero-shot NLI classification of medical abstracts using DeBERTa-v3
Compared SHAP, LIME, occlusion, Input x Gradient, and Attention x Gradient
Measured explanation overlap with the Jaccard index after standardizing top-token attributions
evidence_signal: The study used five enriched hypotheses per diagnostic category and a balanced sample of 1,000 abstracts per class, finding strong performance in clear clinical domains but weaker performance under semantic ambiguity.
watch_item: Explanation outputs may be unstable in overlapping or ambiguous diagnoses, so single-method interpretations can be misleading.
paper_title: A Comparative Explainability Framework for DeBERTa-v3 in Zero-Shot Medical Abstract Classification
